note: XXIV fill shots, recipe B, the sky of 4-6 Oct 1893 · RETAKE of refused beats, 20 Nov
style: An oil painting of 1893, painted alla prima in the manner of Sargent, Atkinson Grimshaw and the Victorian narrative painters: visible loose brushstrokes, thick impasto in the lights, thin transparent glazes in the shadows, soft lost edges, broken colour, canvas weave showing through; pale, cool early-October daylight in England: a low autumn sun a third of the way up the sky, soft silvery light through thin high cloud, long cool shadows, colours muted and slightly grey-green, trees only beginning to turn; the sun just setting: low warm light only along the horizon, the rest cool and grey. Horse-drawn traffic only, no motor cars. Figures small, unidealised. Not an illustration, not digital art. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, lettering, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: Shot: very wide. At sunset on an October evening, a three-masted sailing ship drifts down the Thames past Purfleet on the ebb tide, her sails dark against a thin band of red low on the horizon, the marsh and river grey, a few lights on the shore.

Shot: far, exterior, looking in. The asylum at dusk on an October evening, the sun just gone, the sky grey-violet: through a lit study window a group of men and one woman seated round a table of papers, small.
Shot: very wide. The open North Sea at dusk, a three-masted sailing ship far off running east under full sail, a long low band of fading light on the horizon, grey swell.
